title: DTC-SpMM: Bridging the Gap in Accelerating General Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Tensor Cores
problem: Accelerating general Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) on Tensor Cores requires significant engineering effort, and current techniques exhibit crucial performance gaps. Existing approaches struggle to fully leverage Tensor Cores for general sparse matrix workloads.
motivation: SpMM is a fundamental building-block operation in scientific computing and machine learning applications, and Tensor Cores in modern GPUs offer acceleration opportunities that remain largely untapped.
method: DTC-SpMM makes sparse matrix multiplication run fast on Tensor Cores (GPU units designed for high-speed math) using three coordinated techniques. First, it compresses sparse matrices to skip zeros and save memory. Second, it reorders matrix elements so frequently-used pieces sit close together in memory, speeding retrieval. Third, it optimizes the runtime pipeline—how work flows through the Tensor Cores—to keep them constantly busy. Testing on modern GPUs shows measurable performance improvements across diverse matrix types.
key_novelty: A unified framework for Tensor Cores that combines data compression, matrix reordering, and pipeline tuning for sparse multiplication.
contributions: Comprehensive analysis of state-of-the-art TC-based SpMM and identification of performance gaps
Efficient compression formats optimized for Tensor Core acceleration
Reordering methods to enhance data locality and cache efficiency
Runtime pipeline optimizations and end-to-end speedups in GNN training (1.91×)
primary_theme: Tensor Core Acceleration for Sparse Matrix Multiplication
